item.title: Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics opens in historic first for Africa
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
Photo shows the Olympic rings during the opening ceremony of the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, Oct. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Wei) DAKAR, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games (YOG) opened on Saturday, marking the first time an Olympic event has been held on African soil. The opening ceremony took place at the 55,000-seat Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio, a new city located 30 km from Senegal's capital of Dakar. According to the organizing committee, Khady Niang, the ceremony director, said the show allows Africa to "tell the world who we are, where we come from and where we want to go." The two-hour show started at 6:30 p.m. local time, marked by the arrival of International Olympic Committee President Kirsty Coventry and Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Following the parade of athletes, the spotlight turned to a story of three generations passing the baton from one to the next: Alkebulan, the mother, represented the values of ancestral Africa; her son, Keb, embodied Africa today; and Sitoe, a young Senegalese girl, symbolized hope for the future. The opening act paid tribute to the Africa of the past, immediately electrifying the crowd as Alkebulan rode into the arena on horseback. Iconic instruments, including the sabar, the tama (talking drum) and the djembe, introduced the continent's rich musical heritage, while traditional attire from Mali, Ghana, Senegal and South Africa showcased the diversity of African cultural traditions. The momentum built with performances of Senegal's traditional faux-lion dance and wrestlers' dance, culminating in a finale in which 360 dancers came together to form the map of Africa. In the second act, Keb arrived on a motorcycle in a scene inspired by the Senegalese film Touki Bouki. He led Sitoe and the spectators into the world of contemporary African art, striking a chord with younger generations. As Keb and Sitoe strolled through the streets, a series of artistic performances featuring live painting, music, dance and hip-hop brought the scene to life. The festivities were followed by the parade of flags representing the participating national Olympic committees, with Greece and the Refugee Olympic Team leading the procession and host nation Senegal bringing up the rear. "For years, we have been talking about this moment -- the first Olympic sporting event on African soil and now here we are. This historic moment is for Senegal, for Africa, for our entire Olympic movement, and to all of our young amazing athletes," Coventry said in her speech. "This is the Africa that I am so proud and so excited for the world to experience," she added, voicing hope for young talents to "believe in yourselves, to dream big and to do things you never thought were possible." After Senegalese President Faye officially declared the fourth Summer Youth Olympic Games open, the stadium erupted in vibrant Afrobeats music. The celebration continued with sports demonstrations, a choreographed formation of the Olympic rings and the Dakar 2026 emblem, the Olympic anthem, the raising of the Olympic flag and the solemn reading of the Youth Olympic oath. The much-anticipated lighting of the Olympic cauldron came last. Senegalese fencer Abdourahmane Marieme Sy, 17, and judoka Aicha Diop, 15, jointly carried the final torch, receiving the flame from canoeist Yves Bourhis, triple jumper Sally Sarr and Amadou Dia Ba, Senegal's first and, to date, only Olympic medalist. As the Olympic cauldron was lit, dancers wearing masks and futuristic costumes created a pathway for an Afrofuturism-inspired fashion show. The act also featured a standout performance by a 12-year-old drummer whose solo drew loud applause. At 8:30 p.m., the performers took their final bow, bringing the ceremony to a jubilant close. Held in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly from Oct. 31 to Nov. 13, the fourth edition of the YOG will bring together more than 2,600 athletes from over 200 delegations. A total of 25 sports will feature on the official competition program, alongside 10 engagement sports. Dakar 2026 will also feature the Youth Olympic debuts of wushu, baseball5 and skateboarding, as well as the Refugee Olympic Team's historic first appearance at the Games. China has sent 66 athletes to compete in 21 sports at the Dakar Youth Olympics. Wushu athlete Lin Yilei and swimmer Chang Mohan, both 15, were named China's flagbearers for the opening ceremony. ■ Artists perform during the opening ceremony of the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, Oct. 31, 2026. item.title: China's new rules to protect children's health, safety take effect
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
BEIJING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- Four new or revised mandatory national standards and regulations to better protect children's health and safety took effect in China on Sunday, covering classroom lighting, youth sports training, and children's products and toys. The rules aim to reduce health and safety risks in children's daily learning, physical activities and play, with a greater emphasis on prevention and clearer safety requirements. BETTER LIGHTING TO PROTECT EYESIGHT A revised national standard on classroom lighting and daylighting sets stricter requirements for the lighting environment in primary and secondary schools, as China steps up efforts to curb myopia among children and adolescents. The standard addresses aspects such as natural light, lighting uniformity, blue-light hazards and flicker, aiming to enhance the comfort of classrooms for students who spend long hours reading and writing. It also calls for regular inspections and upkeep of lighting equipment. The revised standard will also apply to secondary vocational schools, while extracurricular training institutions serving school-age children are encouraged to follow its requirements. Liu Yiwei, a lecturer at Capital Normal University, said the new standard sets more detailed mandatory requirements for classroom lighting, providing a measurable and enforceable framework to support efforts to prevent myopia among young students. It incorporates the principle of putting health first into educational settings and places greater emphasis on preventing myopia before it develops, Liu added. MORE STANDARDIZED SPORTS TRAINING A new code of conduct for youth sports training sets requirements for training venues, class sizes, instructor qualifications and safety management, addressing concerns over unsafe facilities and uneven coaching standards in a rapidly growing market. It is essential for training providers to tailor courses to align with the ages, physical conditions, and varying levels of athletic ability of children. Instructors must hold recognized qualifications, while people with specified criminal records, including those involving sexual abuse or physical assault, are prohibited from working in the sector. The rules also establish limits on class sizes and require additional first-aid support for high-risk sports, helping create safer conditions for children to participate in physical activities. Huang Haiyan, dean of the School of Management at Beijing Sport University, noted that the code upgrades the regulatory framework and is a necessary step toward higher-quality development of the industry. The code should serve as a basis for further clarifying the respective oversight responsibilities of education, market regulation and public security authorities, helping improve the overall governance of the industry, Huang said. SAFER CHILDREN'S PRODUCTS, TOYS A new mandatory national standard on the general safety of children's products establishes baseline requirements for products used, worn or played with by children under 14, covering product categories that previously lacked mandatory safety standards. The standard covers risks such as sharp edges, detachable small parts that could cause choking, and cords that could pose strangulation hazards. It also sets limits on potentially harmful chemicals, including heavy metals and formaldehyde. Meanwhile, revised mandatory toy safety standards expand controls on hazardous substances and strengthen requirements concerning physical safety and fire risks. The revisions pay particular attention to products that have drawn public concern, including popular novelty toys such as squishy toys and slime. They introduce additional limits on substances such as formaldehyde, plasticizers and boron, helping reduce the risk of harmful chemical exposure. Together, the new requirements are the country's latest move to fill the safety gaps for certain products used in children's everyday lives, making safety standards more comprehensive as the range of children's goods continues to expand. ■

item.title: Roses honoring two late women who served rural China go on sale
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
KUNMING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- Two Chinese roses named after the women who died while helping rural communities went on sale in China earlier this week, following public calls to honor them with the flowers. One is a gosling-yellow rose called "Wenxiu." The other, "Jiaolong," has soft-pink petals and a faint fragrance. Both were bred by the Flower Research Institute of the Yunnan Academy of Agricultural Sciences and have independently developed Chinese intellectual property rights. "Wenxiu" honors Huang Wenxiu, who returned to her hometown in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region after earning a master's degree in Beijing. She volunteered to work in Baini village of Leye County, helping residents improve their livelihoods. In June 2019, Huang was caught in a flash flood while returning to the village. She died at 30. The pink rose bears the name of He Jiaolong, who once served as deputy head of Zhaosu County in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. She became widely known in 2020 after a video of her riding a horse across snowy grasslands to promote local tourism went viral. She later worked to help Xinjiang farmers sell their produce online. In January this year, she fell from a horse while filming promotional material for an agricultural sales campaign. She died three days later, aged 47. Both roses were named at the suggestion of internet users. During separate online campaigns to select names in late 2025 and early 2026, "Wenxiu" and "Jiaolong" drew widespread support and were adopted by the breeders. The institute later donated rose plants to Guangxi and Xinjiang, where the women had worked. The flowers were developed in Yunnan, China's largest fresh-cut flower producer. The southwestern province produced 22.15 billion stems in 2025, while roughly seven in 10 fresh-cut flowers sold across China come from Yunnan. Yunnan's flower industry also has an international reach. Its fresh-cut flower exports reached 1.22 billion yuan (about 181.7 million U.S. dollars) in 2025, with shipments reaching 64 countries and regions. Despite the industry's scale, Chinese growers have long relied on rose varieties developed overseas. Cai Yanfei, a researcher at the institute, said that producing a new variety takes years of crossbreeding, screening and field observation to ensure its desirable characteristics remain stable. The two varieties went on sale through e-commerce platforms on Thursday. Initial supplies were limited, but more flowers are expected to become available in December, Cai said. For Huang's family, the rose is more than a new commercial variety. In March, her elder sister, Huang Aijuan, traveled to Yunnan to receive the first plants. Wearing a pale-yellow blouse, she held a blooming "Wenxiu" rose in her hands, her eyes filling with tears. "A flower so full of life, bearing Wenxiu's name, is the best tribute to her," she said. ■

item.title: China's "super seller" role expands, benefiting more consumers, businesses
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
GUANGZHOU, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese-made heat pump that could save European households hundreds of euros a year. Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered teaching tools reaching classrooms in Vietnam. Industrial machinery helping developing countries expand production. The 140th China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, is offering a window into how China's exports are giving consumers more choices and businesses access to technology and equipment. When Gree Electric Appliances first attended the Canton Fair 31 years ago, it mainly exported household air conditioners. This year, the Zhuhai-based company is showcasing low-carbon energy solutions covering home appliances, industrial equipment, energy storage and cold-chain technologies. One heat pump system designed for the European market can cut annual electricity use by about 50 percent. At an average European Union electricity price of 0.3 euros per kilowatt-hour, it could save a household in a 150-square-meter home around 800 euros a year, or more than 1,000 euros in countries such as Germany, according to Gree. The company's products now reach more than 200 countries and regions, serving around 600 million consumers. "For Gree, the story of going global is very simple," said Zhu Lei, Gree's vice president and chief marketing officer. "We have one fundamental goal -- to meet consumers' needs and provide them with the best products and services." The potential savings for European households illustrate what Chinese Premier Li Qiang described as the benefits of China's role as a "super seller." "As a 'super seller,' China brings benefits to its trading partners," Li said at the Canton Fair's opening ceremony. He said quality and affordable Chinese goods had raised consumers' actual purchasing power, improved their quality of life, and helped countries strengthen their capacity for industrial development. China exported 23.2 trillion yuan (about 3.46 trillion U.S. dollars) worth of goods in the first nine months of 2026, up 16.4 percent from a year earlier, according to the General Administration of Customs. Its exports range from 300,000-tonne oil tankers and industrial robots to miniature ice makers and portable filming equipment. China's manufacturing supply chains allow businesses to turn ideas into customized products. From 2012 to 2025, China exported about 39 billion U.S. dollars' worth of textile machinery to developing countries, helping some countries in Southeast and South Asia become major textile producers and exporters, according to Chinese industry figures. Marking its 70th anniversary this year, the Canton Fair reflects how China's exports have evolved, offering a wider range of products and technologies to consumers and businesses worldwide. At the first fair in 1957, agricultural products and handicrafts, including silk, tea and porcelain, accounted for 63.9 percent of export transactions by value. Machinery and electronic products became the largest product category in 1999. Today, consumer electronics, AI-powered devices and energy storage equipment are among the products on display. More than 32,000 Chinese and overseas companies are participating in this year's fair, held in three phases in Guangzhou from Oct. 15 to Nov. 4. The first phase drew a record 189,000 overseas buyers from 214 countries and regions. About 64 percent of exhibitors have adopted technologies such as the industrial internet and AI. New products account for 23.2 percent of exhibits and green products for 26 percent, both record shares. At the fair's new energy vehicle exhibition area, GAC Group showcased models that included the AION i60, aimed at overseas consumers concerned about travel costs and driving range. Wei Haigang, president of GAC International, said the company is expanding overseas while building charging and energy storage networks to support local customers. Chinese companies are also bringing technology and services to overseas schools. At the booth of Guangzhou-based CVTE, AI-powered displays turn abstract lessons into visual presentations. Another AI system helps teachers prepare lesson plans, slides and classroom activities. Xiao Hang, president of CVTE's overseas business group, recalled a project in Vietnam in 2024. Rather than simply installing equipment, the company sent a seven-member team to work with local users for three days. "When the children came out of their classrooms, they gathered around us, greeting us in English, Vietnamese and even imperfect Chinese, eager to give us high-fives," Xiao said. "At that moment, we realized this was not just a business, but also a responsibility." Pascal Lamy, former director-general of the World Trade Organization, said the Canton Fair had become a major meeting point for Chinese producers and businesses worldwide, connecting "supply and demand, producers and consumers, ideas and markets." Lamy said China had been one of the greatest beneficiaries of the opening of the world economy over recent decades, while also contributing to the global economy through production, innovation, investment and trade. ■

item.title: China's marriage registration innovations boost the "sweet economy"
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
* China has allowed couples to complete marriage registration at any qualified civil affairs registry nationwide, making it easier for them to combine registration with travel. * Local governments are improving public services for newlyweds, including premarital health checks, marriage-related legal awareness campaigns and wedding consumption vouchers. * By the end of 2025, China had established 1,330 outdoor sites for certificate presentation and 525 marriage registration sites in parks and other landmark locations. NANJING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- Since China removed the requirement that couples register their marriages in the locality of their household registration, local authorities across the country have been exploring new venues and services to make the process more personalized and memorable. From tourist destinations to football stadiums, music festivals and university campuses, young couples are choosing venues of marriage registration that reflect their interests and love stories. Also contributing to this trend is the growth of China's wedding industry and a range of government measures to support marriage, childbirth and child-rearing. ROMANTIC MOMENT As a football fan, Wu Jingyu had never imagined that she and her would-be husband would register their marriage outside a football stadium during a match, exchanging vows and receiving their marriage certificate with the roar of the crowd in the background. "It was truly unforgettable. The passion of watching football blended with the joy and romance of getting married," Wu said, recalling the couple's emotional moment outside the home stadium at a recent Jiangsu Football City League match in the city of Wuxi, east China's Jiangsu Province. A photo wall and red ceremonial platform had been set up outside the stadium as a temporary marriage registration venue. Surrounded by cheering fans and family members, couples completed their formalities in a setting far removed from the conventional government service hall. Such arrangements are emerging across China as local authorities seek to meet the preferences of younger couples and give marriage registration a greater sense of occasion. In Nanjing, a city with around 2,500 years of recorded history in Jiangsu, couples interested in traditional culture can wear Han-style wedding robes and phoenix crowns, along with traditional makeup, for their registration ceremony. Other cities have incorporated marriage registration into music festivals, while some universities have organized group wedding ceremonies for alumni returning to their campuses. By the end of 2025, China had established 1,330 outdoor sites for certificate presentation and 525 marriage registration sites in parks and other landmark locations, according to the Ministry of Civil Affairs. "Younger Chinese are exercising greater autonomy in their views on love and marriage," said Zhou Yongbo, a professor at Soochow University in Jiangsu. "They value not only the marriage certificate but also a personalized experience, a sense of ceremony and memories they can cherish." THE "SWEET ECONOMY" Since May 2025, China has allowed couples to complete marriage registration at any qualified civil affairs registry nationwide, making it easier for them to combine registration with travel. In Lijiang, southwest China's Yunnan Province, a couple exchanged vows in front of the snow-capped Yulong Snow Mountain, framed by a heart-shaped arch of white roses. This province's tourism and cut-flower industries give it natural advantages as a destination-wedding choice, and local scenic areas and wedding companies have moved quickly to build a mature industry. Yang Libin, head of a wedding planning company in Yunnan with over a decade of experience, began focusing on customized destination weddings in 2025. His team uses questionnaires and consultations to learn about couples' stories and preferences before selecting venues and designing ceremonies. "Professional services should improve the couples' experience and make every wedding unique," Yang said. In the first year after their shift of focus, his company organized more than 280 destination weddings. The wedding photography industry is another major part of the "sweet economy." In Lijiang, industry associations have introduced service standards covering makeup, clothing, photo production and after-sales support. Packages costing around 10,000 yuan (about 1,500 U.S. dollars) can include costumes, makeup, private transport and accommodation. By integrating photography, ceremonies and honeymoon travel, Lijiang attracted more than 140,000 couples in 2025, with its wedding industry market exceeding 1.1 billion yuan. In Dali, another popular Yunnan destination, businesses have developed over 30 wedding settings, including lakeside lawns and traditional Bai ethnic courtyards, drawing on the area's Cangshan Mountain and Erhai Lake. Wang Yu, a groom from Hebei Province in north China, and his wife held their ceremony in the morning and took wedding photos near Erhai Lake in the afternoon, while relatives and friends visited nearby attractions. "There were no complicated formalities, and we could combine getting married with traveling. It has been a great experience." IMPROVED PUBLIC SERVICES While simplifying registration procedures, local governments are also improving services for newlyweds. In Haidian District of Beijing, for example, its maternal and child health care hospital has set up a premarital health center inside the district's marriage registration office. Newlyweds can complete a premarital health check and marriage registration in the same building and on the same day. In Chengdu, capital of southwest China's Sichuan Province, a team from the local court has worked with marriage registration offices on multiple occasions during peak registration periods, giving newlyweds legal handbooks on marriage and family, Civil Code brochures, and briefings on spousal rights, joint property and family dispute resolution. This effort is part of a broader push to embed legal education into the registration process. Many localities have even introduced marriage incentives and wedding consumption vouchers to help newlyweds manage expenses. Also, many provincial-level regions have extended marriage leave, with the longest reaching 30 days. Local governments are seeking to link the development of the "sweet economy" with efforts to create a more supportive environment for marriage, childbirth and child-rearing. In 2025, China introduced 23 measures to support childbirth and child-rearing. Multiple regions have made childbirth-related medical expenses largely or entirely free for families, while Jiangsu has introduced childcare service vouchers. Zhou added that localities are pairing the new registration settings with premarital education and legal consultation, which helps young people understand the rights and obligations of marriage and avoid registering on impulse. "The business of romance is closely connected to people's aspirations for a better life," he said. "As society places greater emphasis on creating a family-friendly environment, preserving that sweetness requires continued innovation in public services." ■

item.title: Small producers, big markets -- the CIIE story
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
by Maya Majueran At a time when global trade is increasingly disturbed by tariffs, protectionism and geopolitical competition, a different story is emerging from Shanghai's exhibition halls. It is not about multinational giants or the strategic interests of major economies. It is about Peruvian artisans, Kenyan avocado farmers and Malagasy herders -- ordinary producers seeking access to international markets and opportunities to improve their livelihoods. The China International Import Expo (CIIE) is helping turn "inclusive globalization" from a diplomatic slogan into economic reality by creating market opportunities, generating employment, and improving livelihoods. For many developing countries, the greatest obstacle to international trade is not a lack of products or entrepreneurial ambition, but limited access to markets, financing, logistics and commercial networks. Through targeted support, dedicated exhibition areas for least-developed countries, and direct connections with Chinese buyers, the CIIE seeks to reduce these barriers. The objective is not charity, but meaningful participation in global trade. The CIIE's significance also lies in its continuity. Through its "6 days + 365 days" model, the expo connects temporary exhibitions with year-round trading platforms. Bonded warehousing, cross-border e-commerce, and buyer matchmaking help businesses turn initial orders into sustained commercial relationships. In July 2025, Burundi shipped 38.4 tonnes of Arabica coffee directly to China for the first time, followed by contracts exceeding 900 tonnes worth over 5 million U.S. dollars. At the seventh CIIE in 2024, 13 of 16 participating Nigerian companies reportedly secured agreements, including a cocoa contract worth over 1.2 million dollars. The eighth CIIE last year recorded 83.49 billion dollars in one-year intended deals, up 4.4 percent from the previous edition and hitting a new high. Smaller economies face structural disadvantages in international trade. Regulatory compliance, logistics, marketing, and distribution impose disproportionately high costs on low-volume exporters. By connecting buyers and sellers and facilitating market entry, the CIIE helps reduce these barriers. The CIIE offers one practical model for smaller economies to access international markets. For artisans in Peru, farmers in Kenya, and herding communities in Madagascar, the benefits can extend beyond export contracts to employment, household incomes and local development. Inclusive globalization should be measured not simply by how much trade expands, but by how widely its opportunities are shared. It is an approach worth drawing on. Editor's note: Maya Majueran serves as the director of the Belt and Road Initiative Sri Lanka, an independent and pioneering organization with strong expertise in Belt and Road Initiative advice and support. The views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect those of Xinhua News Agency.■

item.title: Protocol upgrading China-Peru FTA takes effect
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
BEIJING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- The protocol upgrading the China-Peru free trade agreement (FTA) took effect on Sunday, according to China's Ministry of Commerce (MOC). China and Peru launched negotiations on the upgrade in November 2018 and signed the protocol on Nov. 14, 2024. The original FTA was signed in 2009 and took effect in 2010. The protocol improves seven existing chapters of the original FTA, covering rules of origin, customs procedures and trade facilitation, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, intellectual property rights, trade in services, temporary entry of business personnel, and investment, the MOC said in an online statement. The protocol also adds five new chapters on standards and conformity assessment cooperation, competition policy, e-commerce, global supply chains, and environment and trade. The two sides also set out future provisions for negotiations on negative lists for trade in services and investment, aimed at further raising openness in these areas, according to the statement. The China-Peru FTA was the first comprehensive free trade agreement China signed with a Latin American country. China is Peru's largest trading partner, largest export market and largest source of imports, while Peru is China's fourth-largest trading partner in Latin America and an important investment destination, said an MOC official. Under the protocol, the new chapter on global supply chains encourages multimodal transport and the development of foreign trade logistics corridors and infrastructure, an innovative arrangement that signals the two countries' commitment to keeping supply chains stable and unimpeded. The chapter on standards and conformity assessment cooperation establishes a dedicated cooperation mechanism and sets out an intended cooperation list, creating a platform for mutual recognition of standards that is expected to reduce trade costs for enterprises. The two sides agreed to launch negotiations on negative lists for trade in services and investment within two years after the protocol takes effect, in a bid to further raise the level of openness in these areas and continue to tap the potential of bilateral trade and investment, the official added. Since the original FTA came into force in 2010, it has played an important role in promoting bilateral economic and trade cooperation. Two-way trade rose from 6.4 billion U.S. dollars in 2009 to 50.4 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, an increase of nearly seven times, official data show. The protocol is expected to help tap further opportunities for bilateral trade and investment cooperation, provide a better business environment for enterprises of both countries and inject new vitality into bilateral economic and trade relations, the MOC said. ■

item.title: Building a strong Party for a strong China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
"Rigorous self-governance strengthens the Party, by building the confidence of the people," said an American writer who has been living in China for over 20 years. At a plenum that concluded Thursday, the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee adopted a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, stressing the need to maintain a tough stance against corruption and strengthen checks on and oversight over the exercise of power. Since its founding in 1921, the CPC has grown from just over 50 members to the world's largest governing party. How does a party of this scale ensure strict self-governance? What measures has it put in place, and what results has it delivered?

BEIJING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- The Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance was made public on Sunday. The document was adopted at the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee on Oct. 29. Please see the attachment for the English translation of the full text of this document. ■
